literal: those who renounced / greatness / measure / if told / of the world / the dead / having counted / having taken / like that
translation: To measure and state the greatness of those who have renounced is like trying to count the dead of the world.
modern: ஆசைகளைத் துறந்தவர்களின் பெருமையை அளவிட்டுச் சொல்வது, இந்த உலகத்தில் இதுவரை இறந்துபோனவர்களை எண்ணிக் கணக்கிடுவதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the boundless nature of an ascetic's greatness through a striking comparison. The word 'துறந்தார்' refers to those who have renounced worldly attachments, and 'பெருமை' denotes their resulting greatness. The poet says that trying to measure ('துணை கூறின்') this greatness is as impossible as counting ('எண்ணிக்கொண்டு') all the people who have ever died ('இறந்தாரை') in the world ('வையத்து'). Just as the number of the dead is infinite and beyond human calculation, the virtues and spiritual power of true renouncers cannot be quantified.
